clue.text: Hopes when religious right embraces void

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
pi is short for pious, so religious

indicators.note: voiding a word empties out its middle, leaving only the outside letters of the word embraces

explanation.surface: A political worry: what someone hopes for when the religious right takes hold of a vacuum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' looks like a containment signal, but it is the word that is emptied by 'void', leaving its outer letters ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have ambitions, so hopes and aspires are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Gaming stake big smoker raised

indicators.note: raised in a down light means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Etna is a large active volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A heavy smoker raises the stakes at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big smoker' is not a person but the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake put in before cards are dealt in poker.

clue.text: One at the game longer after work's over

indicators.note: after puts the longer piece behind the work piece
over means turned over, so the letters for work are reversed

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an acher is one who longs or aches

explanation.surface: Someone at a game who longs for it once work is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the game' means engaged in taking game birds or animals illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: A poacher illegally takes game, so is one at the game.

clue.text: One following religion of God's volunteers

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god, plus S from the possessive
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A follower of a faith belonging to God's volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a Rastafarian, an adherent of the Rastafari religion.

clue.text: Makes breathless male distinct among Nazi guards

indicators.note: among puts the middle pieces between the guards' letters

parts.note: the SS were Nazi guards
other means different or distinct

explanation.surface: A man stands out among Nazi guards and is left gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother is to suffocate, to stop someone breathing.

clue.text: Song about deceiver in rural idyll

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song's letters go round the deceiver's

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, a deceiver

explanation.surface: A ballad about a seducer set in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of Greece, became the poetic byword for an unspoiled pastoral paradise.

clue.text: Car runs, passing Henry Ford, for example

indicators.note: passing here means going around, so the car's letters enclose Henry

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A car runs past Henry Ford, the car maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry Ford' tempts as one name; 'Ford' alone is the definition, meaning the novelist Ford Madox Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford was an English novelist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Getting on N66 with a boarding pass

indicators.note: boarding means getting inside, so these pieces go into the pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
N stays N and 66 in Roman numerals is VI VI

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard the N66 bus with a boarding pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' looks like boarding a bus, but means getting along well.
explanation.definitionFit: Convivial means friendly and sociable, like people who are getting on together.

clue.text: Layer is raised in storehouse

indicators.note: in puts the raised word inside the storehouse

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: raised in a down light means written upwards, so reversed

explanation.surface: A layer is lifted inside a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a layer of material laid down, as sediment or ore.

clue.text: Finally cobbling size seventeens?

definitions.meaning: in the end, after a wait
a cobbler shapes shoes on a last, and giant feet need a lengthy one

explanation.surface: A cobbler at last gets round to making enormous shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, and read literally describes a lengthy shoemaker's form.

clue.text: Rolled small piano inside wrong entrance

indicators.note: inside places the first pieces within the letters for wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
ran, as a ball rolled or ran along
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano on castors rolled through the wrong door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a noun meaning a door, but it is the verb, to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with emotion, to enrapture them.

clue.text: North-eastern China's mountainous region

parts.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate), so pal

explanation.surface: A description of a hilly area in the north-east of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country, home to Everest, so a mountainous region.

clue.text: Scrubland bird indeed with name that's crazily complicated

parts.note: a heath is open scrubby land
a robin is a bird
so, as in 'it is so!', meaning indeed

explanation.surface: A nature note: a bird on the heath, with a name that is absurdly involved.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famous for drawing absurdly elaborate contraptions, so his name became an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Heath Robinson describes a contraption that is ingenious but absurdly over-elaborate.

clue.text: It's remarkable: Post Office people performing rounds without women

indicators.note: without means outside, so Post Office goes round the women

parts.note: PO is the Post Office
hen means a woman, as in a hen party
men means people
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Postal workers doing their rounds with no women among them is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' only completes the picture of postmen at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is a remarkable person or thing, a marvel.

clue.text: Lyre hard to play? It's that business with the arms!

indicators.note: playing with letters means jumbling them into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician complains a lyre is hard to play with one's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' here means coats of arms, not limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry is the study and design of coats of arms, the business of armorial bearings.

clue.text: See good chap over in valley who the focus of attention?

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: in puts the saint and over inside the valley

parts.note: a dene is a small wooded valley
ST is a saint, a good person
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A good fellow in a valley asks who is attracting attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the cryptic definition: what draws attention is literally a magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is a natural magnet, something that attracts, figuratively a centre of attention.

clue.text: Weapon's first round in place

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the abbreviation for place

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
first is written 1st, read as IST
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A weapon's first round fired in a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a handgun, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Upright swimmer said to visit bay for example

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for visiting is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: see, as to see a doctor
a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: An upright swimmer is reported to visit a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like part of the coast, but it is a horse's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A seahorse is a fish that swims vertically, an upright swimmer.

clue.text: US inventor travels back to bring game over

indicators.note: travelling back means the inventor's name is read from end to start

parts.note: Thomas Edison was a prolific American inventor

explanation.surface: An American inventor goes back in time to finish a game.
explanation.walkthrough: No side is the referee's call ending a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, no-side is the end of the match, when the game is over.

clue.text: Close to tears, top fashion designer thoroughly upset

indicators.note: close means the end, so the last letter of tears

parts.note: a hatter makes hats, which are tops

explanation.surface: A leading fashion designer is in tears and badly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top fashion' looks like high fashion, but a top is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shattered is to be thoroughly upset, so to shatter is to upset deeply.

clue.text: Ecstasy girl held by policeman makes confession

indicators.note: held by means the girl's letters sit inside the policeman's

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Clare is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl with drugs is arrested by an officer and owns up.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to state it openly, to admit or confess it.

clue.text: Pattern entrenched in mechanical routine

indicators.note: in places the entrenched word inside the routine

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition
set means fixed firmly, entrenched

explanation.surface: A design becomes fixed in an unthinking habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rose-shaped decorative pattern or ornament.

clue.text: Quick to doze off during watch, secretly

indicators.note: during means within, so the doze goes inside the watching

parts.note: to spy is to watch covertly
to nap is to doze

explanation.surface: Someone is quick to drop off while secretly on watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means brisk or fast, as in 'make it snappy'.

clue.text: Bananas one mashes well — provision that seniors may consume?

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone mashing bananas well, as food for the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit to be mashed, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals on wheels is a service delivering hot food to elderly people at home.

clue.text: The French in their way sent up Swiss scientist

indicators.note: in sets the French article inside the reversed street
sent up in a down light means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: rue is French for street, so their way
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people in their own way mock a Swiss scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to the French, so their way is a French street, RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was a Swiss mathematician and physicist.

clue.text: Northerner gets drunk touring clubs

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the drunk encloses clubs

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A northerner gets drunk on a tour of nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, in the north of Britain.

clue.text: Explosive in yellow container overturned!

indicators.note: overturned in a down light means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A bomb in a yellow canister has been knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitro is short for nitroglycerine, a powerful explosive.

clue.text: Still very drunk

definitions.meaning: slang for so drunk as to be incapable

explanation.surface: Someone remains extremely drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralytic means paralysed, so motionless, and in British slang hopelessly intoxicated.

clue.text: No pressure on accountant in City here growth's assured

indicators.note: in sets the trimmed accountant inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York City

indicators.note: No tells us to drop the letter for pressure

parts.note: a purser keeps the accounts on a ship
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An accountant working in a city free of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No pressure' removes P from PURSER, leaving URSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is where young plants are raised, a place where growth is assured.

clue.text: Firm answer man accepts

indicators.note: accepts means the man's name takes in the letter for answer

parts.note: Ernest is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man gives a firm answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and resolute, and firm can mean the same steadfastness.
